_about.description: Curated local subset of MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise techniques used for offline TTP mapping. Technique IDs and names are from the public MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base; descriptions here are short paraphrases written for this project, not verbatim MITRE text.
_about.attribution: MITRE ATT&CK is a registered trademark of The MITRE Corporation. See https://attack.mitre.org/
_about.coverage: Subset only. This file covers the threat categories handled by this prototype and is not a complete ATT&CK export.

command_and_control.description: Adversary communicates with compromised hosts over common protocols so the traffic blends with normal activity.
Command traffic is encrypted to hide its content from network inspection.

phishing.description: Adversary sends deceptive messages to obtain credentials or deliver a malicious payload.
The intrusion depends on a user opening a file or following a link.

malware_delivery.description: Additional tools or payloads are transferred onto a host from an external system.
Delivery succeeds only when the target runs the supplied file.

scanning.description: Adversary probes hosts and services to identify reachable systems and exposed ports.
Services running on remote hosts are enumerated to find exploitable entry points.

brute_force.description: Repeated authentication attempts are made to guess valid credentials.
Credentials obtained by guessing are then used as legitimate logins.

data_exfiltration.description: Collected data is sent out through the same channel used for command traffic.
Data leaves the network over a protocol separate from the main command channel.

botnet.description: Adversary obtains a network of compromised hosts to support later operations.
Compromised hosts generate traffic intended to exhaust a target's availability.

unknown.description: Assigned as a default when the observed behaviour is not yet attributable to a specific technique.
